newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan FGEP group buys 54,000T US corn at tender.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan FGEP group buys 54,000T US corn at tender.

text.p: Taiwan's FGEP corn-buying group bought one 54,000-tonne shipment of U.S. No.2 corn from Mitsubishi Corp at a tender on Thursday, traders said.

Thursday's tender marked Taiwan's first return to the world corn market since the government reported an epidemic of hog foot and mouth disease on March 20 and ordered a pork export ban and islandwide drive to slaughter or inoculate 14 million hogs.
Taiwan importers have cancelled several corn tenders and at least one purchased shipment in the wake of the announcement as the mass slaughter slashed demand for feed corn.
A buyer at the group said it was lured back into the market by sharp recent rises in U.S. wheat prices, which importers feared could in turn push corn prices higher.
The group delayed the shipment for five days during the tender due to special requests by some of the group's buyers.
The shipment was slated for delivery from the U.S. Gulf of Mexico from June 25 to July 10, but now delayed for five days.
The FGEP group comprises Fwu Sow Grain, Great Wall Enterprise, President Enterprise, Ever Smile Feed Mill Co and Fong Yu.
